title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a handwritten note. It is a typed page, numbered '- 64 -' and headed 'IX', with a stamped '382'. It appears to be a page of the typescript of SGA 7, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §5, which has ended up in the folder of handwritten notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. The neighbouring pages deal with something unrelated: endomorphisms of divided-power differential algebras k{T}{X0,X1,dX0,dX1}/(X0+X1−T, dX0+dX1) that are compatible with two augmentations α and β.

The mathematics is as follows.

- **Setting.** S is a henselian trait (henselian discrete valuation ring) with fraction field K and residue characteristic p. A_K is an abelian variety over K with semistable reduction, and A is its Néron model, with identity component A^o.
- **Tate module and fixed part.** For a prime ℓ, the Tate module X_η = T_ℓ(A_K) is viewed as a pro-ℓ Barsotti–Tate group over K. Its 'fixed part' X_η^f is the generic fibre of the pro-ℓ Barsotti–Tate group X^f = T_ℓ(A^o)^f over S. This comes from the 'finite' part of the groups A^o[ℓ^n], i.e. the part that extends over S.
- **Theorem 5.8 (Raynaud).** Assume char K = 0 when ℓ = p, so that Tate's theorem [33, th. 4] is available: on p-divisible groups over S, passing to the generic fibre is fully faithful. Then for every pro-ℓ Barsotti–Tate group F over S, every homomorphism F_η → X_η factors through X_η^f.
- **Role of the theorem.** It gives an intrinsic characterisation of the fixed part, in terms of the Barsotti–Tate structure alone: X_η^f is the largest part of X_η receiving all maps from generic fibres of Barsotti–Tate groups over S. This is stronger than 5.7.
- **Corollary 5.9.** Pass to the associated ind-ℓ groups and use Tate's theorem again. Then every homomorphism u_η : F_η → A_η, with F an ind-ℓ Barsotti–Tate group over S, extends uniquely to u : F → A.
- **Meaning.** The Néron mapping property (1.1.2) holds for Barsotti–Tate ind-group schemes, even though these are not smooth. Only the ind-étale case would follow directly from the definition of the Néron model.
errors: Minor wording: A_K is called a 'schéma abélien' over the field K; an abelian variety over K is meant.
Tate's theorem as originally stated is for complete discrete valuation rings. Its use over a henselian trait presupposes a standard reduction to the complete case, which the page leaves implicit.

ideas.what: Homomorphisms from generic fibres of Barsotti–Tate groups over S into T_ℓ(A_K) factor through the fixed part (Raynaud's theorem).
ideas.modern_name: Characterisation of the finite/fixed part of the p-divisible group of a semistable abelian variety; Néron-type extension property for p-divisible groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Raynaud (as stated in SGA 7 IX, Th. 5.8)
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, §5, Théorème 5.8 (Springer LNM 288, 1972)

ideas.what: Néron mapping property extended to ind-ℓ Barsotti–Tate groups (non-smooth), via Tate's full faithfulness theorem.
Use of Tate's theorem that the generic-fibre functor on p-divisible groups is fully faithful in mixed characteristic.
ideas.modern_name: Tate's full faithfulness theorem for p-divisible groups
ideas.where_published: Cited in SGA 7 IX as [33, th. 4]

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of SGA 7 Exposé IX, whose content (Th. 5.8 and Cor. 5.9) is published and credited to Raynaud and Grothendieck. It is only filed among the PD de Rham notes, has no mathematical link to the neighbouring handwritten pages, and contains nothing unpublished.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially accurate.
In the line beginning 'qui est la fibre générique', the image reads 'X^f = T_ℓ(A^o)^f'; the superscript o is the identity-component marker.
The stamped '382' and the handwritten '188' in the margin are archive/pagination marks, not mathematical content.
